artworks.title: Tiresias Transformed into a Woman
artworks.description: Della Vecchia paints Tiresias' sex-change — the Theban seer whose mother Chariclo is Athena's favorite nymph in the parallel blinding myth. Not Chariclo wife of Chiron.

artworks.title: Teiresias Foretells the Future to Odysseus
artworks.description: Fuseli's Nekyia: the shade of Tiresias speaks to Odysseus — Chariclo's son as the underworld prophet Homer made immortal.

popCulture.title: Tiresias
popCulture.description: Chariclo's son — the Theban prophet blinded (in one tradition) when he saw Athena bathing, while his mother begged the goddess for mercy.

popCulture.title: Athena
popCulture.description: Chariclo's divine companion — the goddess who blinds Tiresias and, at Chariclo's plea, grants him prophecy and a staff in Callimachus' hymn.

popCulture.title: Callimachus
popCulture.creator: Callimachus
popCulture.description: Callimachus' Hymn 5 (The Bath of Pallas) stages Athena bathing with Chariclo when Tiresias looks — the Hellenistic telling that makes the mother the goddess's intimate.
